description:
The reactive component base every Noodloft component is built on: a model, a DTO, a pure
            evaluator, and a three-state result that tells a no-op apart from a refusal. No dependencies.
releaseNotes:
### Added

- **A `States` family, and an `AnimationDirector2D` on top of it.** Several sources competing for one
  exclusive output, arbitrated so that exactly one wins and the winner is announced once.

  The case that produced it: an entity whose locomotion, hit reaction and death each called `Play` on
  the same `AnimatedSprite2D`. Whichever ran last won, so a killing blow — which raises `OnDamaged`
  and then `OnDied` — started the death animation and then let the hit animation finish underneath it,
  releasing back to idle. The corpse stood up. Neither component was wrong on its own, which is why
  this is arbitration and not a bug fix.

  It is the same rule the camera nodes follow by being the camera rather than driving one: **one
  writer per output**. A camera can enforce that structurally by owning the transform; an animator has
  several genuinely independent sources, so it has to be explicit.

  - `StateArbiterReactiveComponent`, `StateRequest`, `ArbitrationOperation`,
    `DefaultStateArbiterEvaluator`, `StateArbiterDefinition` — engine-agnostic and tested without an
    engine. Nothing in it is animation-specific; it arbitrates any exclusive output.

  - **A claim holds until its source changes or releases it.** That one rule covers both shapes a game
    needs with nothing to configure: an ongoing truth re-asserted whenever it changes, and a
    run-to-completion claim set on an event and dropped when the animation ends. An earlier draft had
    a `Latched` flag for the second; it turned out to be describing the same behaviour twice.

  - **Ties go to whoever claimed first.** "Whoever asked last" is precisely the rule that makes two
    equal-priority sources swap every frame, which is the flicker the component exists to prevent.
    Updating a claim keeps its original position, so a source does not lose a tie it used to win purely
    by changing its mind.

  - **Re-claiming the same thing is `Unchanged` and silent**, so a source may assert every frame rather
    than track its own changes. `Retrigger` exists for the other case — a second hit landing during a
    flinch should restart it — and it is a real operation rather than a flag, because "pretend this
    changed" would make `Applied` mean something different here than everywhere else. It bumps a
    `Generation` on the model, and only when the retriggering source is actually the winner: a hit
    retriggered under a death animation must restart neither.

  - `AnimationDirector2D` binds it to an `AnimatedSprite2D` with two verbs — `Hold` for an ongoing
    truth, `PlayOnce` for a one-shot that releases itself when the animation finishes. A one-shot
    claimed under something higher waits rather than vanishing, so an attack swing overlapped by a
    flinch still runs. It checks `SpriteFrames.HasAnimation` before playing and warns once per unknown
    name, because Godot's own error fires per call and a state re-entered every frame buries the log.

  - `StateArbiterResource` for authoring the fallback in the inspector.

### Notes

- Not saveable, deliberately, alongside the input buffer and the camera shake: it describes this
  instant. Restoring an entity mid-flinch into a world where nothing hit anybody leaves it stuck in one.
